cases.title: Admin endpoints and bad tokens
cases.question: the toggle endpoint, a migration endpoint, and searches with no, forged, alg:none and expired tokens
cases.why: The toggle endpoint needs an admin token even with every toggle off, or anyone could switch the protection off. A token that is sent is always verified, so the forged one fails even with identity off. With identity on, no token, a bad signature, alg none and an expired token are all 401.

cases.why: The question is redacted wherever the service stores it or sends it away (the audit log, the web provider), whatever the toggle. With pii_redaction on, the agents also work from the redacted question: before the first LLM call they ask the router's /guardrails/check, which returns the question masked, and they search and prompt with that. So the LLM provider never sees the email or the card number. A plain /search still uses the real words, because the shards need them to find anything and keep nothing.

cases.why: Indirect injection: the user asked an honest question, and a stored passage carries the attack. With the guard on, the router cuts the trigger phrases out of the passage before returning it. The rest of the sentence (the JSON it wants the model to copy) stays: the rule removes known phrases, it does not understand intent. On the real run, the provider's own content filter refused the unprotected prompt (HTTP 400), a second layer outside this service. It also means one poisoned passage makes every agent call that retrieves it fail. With the guard on, the prompt passed, and the model did not pick the poisoned passage in its top 3.

cases.why: Nothing about a cookie question is harmful, so only the corpus can tell: its best dense match scores 0.4206, below the 0.4421 calibrated for this model. Without the check, every off-topic question costs a search and the agent's LLM tokens on passages that can't answer it. On the real run: 2 LLM calls, 1906 input tokens, $0.00225 without the check; 1 call, 234 input tokens, $0.00049 with it. Blocked, the agent still makes one call on "(no results)", which is the next thing to fix: stop the agent when the router says blocked.
